svg.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', system-ui, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: TheYard's two sites: two names at Wix, one Netlify edge, two web apps and the rendering service on one App Service plan on Azure, and both stores behind both
svg.text: TheYard's two sites: two names, one edge, three web apps on one plan, both stores behind both

A request reads left to right. The name a visitor typed and the path are what differ until the edge; the edge sends a page to the rendering service and everything else to that site's API, and each site opens both stores.
The names, at Wix DNS
Three CNAMEs and one A record, all at the same edge.
One edge: the Netlify site theyard-edge
Terminates HTTPS, then proxies by Host. Three files in this repository.
Azure: RG-THEYARD-SS, one App Service plan in westus3
Three web apps on one machine: two sites on one image, and the service; both stores open.
theyard.stevenstout.biz
CNAME -> theyard-edge.netlify.app, TTL 30 min
The live site, the name a resume carries.
The web app behind it serves Azure SQL
Database by default.
theyard-cosmos.stevenstout.biz
CNAME -> theyard-edge.netlify.app, TTL 30 min
The second site, since 1.0.0.100. One
label, so any DNS form accepts it.
stevenstout.biz and www
A 75.2.60.5 and CNAME -> theyard-edge.netlify.app
Both forward to the live site with a 301,
so a trimmed or retyped address still
lands on the app.
One certificate
Let's Encrypt, issued and renewed by Netlify
Four names on it: the bare domain, www, theyard
and theyard-cosmos. Adding the alias reissued it
within the minute; nothing was bought.
edge/_redirects: the name and the path pick the origin
the first matching rule wins, top to bottom
https://theyard-cosmos.stevenstout.biz/ to the
rendering service as /site/cosmos, 200!
https://theyard-cosmos.stevenstout.biz/* to the
second web app, 200!
/ to the rendering service as /site/sql, 200!
/* to the first web app, 200! (the catch-all,
last)
stevenstout.biz and www: 301 to
theyard.stevenstout.biz
A page is the bare path with its query, so the two
bare-path rules send every page to the service and
the query goes with the rewrite; /index.html is
still the API's own page, drawn in the browser.
netlify.toml: build only when the edge moves
ignore = "git diff --quiet ... -- edge/ netlify.toml"
An application push costs no credits; an edge
change is one deploy, 15 of the month's 300. This
one cost exactly that, read off the meter.
APP-THEYARD-SS-ZMNETJ67BN5H2
https://app-theyard-ss-zmnetj67bn5h2.azurewebsites.net
Store__Default = sql. Peer__Site =
https://theyard-cosmos.stevenstout.biz. Rolled
by the Deploy workflow. A web app for containers
on PLAN-THEYARD-SS.
APP-THEYARD-COSMOS-SS-ZMNETJ67BN5H2
https://app-theyard-cosmos-ss-zmnetj67bn5h2.azurewebsites.net
Store__Default = cosmos. Peer__Site =
https://theyard.stevenstout.biz. Rolled by
Deploy Cosmos. Same image, same plan: one Linux
B2, 2 vCPU and 3.5 GB shared by both sites and
the rendering service, $24.82 a month.
APP-THEYARD-RENDER-SS-ZMNETJ67BN5H2
https://app-theyard-render-ss-zmnetj67bn5h2.azurewebsites.net
The rendering service, one process for both
sites: /site/sql draws for the first,
/site/cosmos for the second. Its own image
(render/Dockerfile: the build on Node, nothing
else), rolled by Deploy Render on the same push.
YARD_SITES names each site's API; a page is read
from that API and drawn, then sent with its data
in it. It opens no store.
Azure SQL Database
Entra-only, no SQL login
Reached as the managed
identity. West US 3,
the plan's own region.
Azure Cosmos DB
no keys on the account
Reached as the managed
identity. West US 2,
one region from the
plan.
HTTPS, then the Host header picks the rule
everything else on theyard: HTTPS to the first web app
everything else on theyard-cosmos: HTTPS to the second web app
a page on either name: HTTPS to the rendering service, as that site
reads the page, the build and the view from that site's API, cookie forwarded
both sites open both stores, as their managed identity; the service opens neither
the Store bar: each site links to the other, at the same page
Each site is one store's site: the web app's default store serves it; a measurement can name the other store for one request with the X-Yard-Store header.
The edge retires at the registrar transfer around the end of October 2026; both names then become two records at Cloudflare, and a Worker takes the rendering function with it.
Source: docs/images/two-sites.svg in the repository, drawn by docs/images/two-sites.mjs and redrawn when a name, a rule or a site changes.
